about: Simulated students for the bench (R-01). Each is a rule, not a learner: a gap on a node makes every problem on that node, and on any node that needs it, wrong until that node is taught; a slip is one known wrong move (web/src/content/slips.json) made every time until its repair; everything else is answered right. 'expected.found' is the gap the mock primer should name (its gap_found hypothesis), null when there is none to find; 'note' says why it differs from what was planted. Plain JSON so the Python bench (src/platy/evaluation) can run the same students.

expected.note: A slip, not a gap: one probe passes, then the repair and a fresh problem.
A one-step slip on line 2 of a two-step problem: one probe passes, then the one-step repair.
The gap is found and taught first; the slip still shows on the way back and gets its repair.
The deeper gap is found. The mock never probes again after teaching, so the one-step gap is never named: the session stalls on misses. A limit of the mock to carry into the real policy.

Three levels below two-step equations. The mock probes two levels down and names the deepest miss, so this gap is misdiagnosed as inverse operations and the explanation doesn't land. R-01 says one to two levels; a real policy needs a rule for a miss on the deepest probe.
